subject: URGENT: Medispan production latency & 5xx spike (EastUS) — cross-region evacuation request
messages:
From: ops@medispan.com
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike - EastUS cluster

Hi Soojin / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden, sustained latency increase and a rapid rise in 5xx responses from our EastUS endpoints starting ~09:00 PDT. Throughput appears to cap while user-facing latency jumps to 2-6s for several API paths. We're also seeing KV cache miss storms in the attached logs.

Impact: customer-facing app errors and queued requests in payment flow. We have partially degraded UI and need an emergency mitigation plan.

Can Redwood initiate cross-region failover to another healthy region (we prefer WestUS2) and open a bridge? Please confirm scope, expected rollback plan, and whether this will require an exec approval. Logs/heatmap attached (medispan-error-sample-0521.log, traffic-heatmap-eastus-0521.png).

--
Sarah Kim
Ops Lead, Medispan
ops@medispan.com
From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: ops@medispan.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike - EastUS cluster

Thanks Sarah — we see the same telemetry on our side and are treating this as P0. Acknowledged and we will coordinate an immediate mitigation. Current assessment (quick): KV-cache saturation + amplification in streaming requests under higher concurrency.

Planned immediate actions (will start now):
- Spin up warm capacity in WestUS2 and pre-warm model shards (15–20 min expected).
- Gradual traffic shift: start with 20% traffic diversion to WestUS2 for 10m, observe errors/latency, then ramp to 50% if stable.
- Enable aggressive KV-prefix caching + transient TTL extension to reduce cold misses during migration.

We need permission to execute the partial traffic shift and to run the cache TTL tweak. We'll monitor with you on the bridge. I'm attaching our runbook v2 for evacuation steps (runbook-eastus-evacuation-v2.md).

If Medispan prefers a hard cutover instead of a gradual ramp, please confirm ASAP — hard cutover has higher client-side reconnection risk.

I'll open a Slack bridge (CRT) and keep Laura (SRE) and Marissa (AM) in the loop.

— Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medispan.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-21T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike - EastUS cluster

We ran a quick heap/profile on the EastUS serving cluster and are seeing a KV-cache eviction cascade: large prefix churn causing repeated decoder warmups and blocking IO. Symptoms line up with the customer's logs.

Operational plan (implementation details):
1) Start WestUS2 capacity: allocate 4x serving instances with warmed weights and KV cache pre-populated from snapshot (ETA ~12 min).
2) Traffic steering: use weighted routing via SmartRouter — start at 20% WestUS2 for 10m, then 50% for 15m if 5xx/latency <= 1.2x baseline.
3) Apply temporary TTL extension + keepalive for hot prefixes (reduces miss rate).
4) If errors persist after ramp, pause and rollback to EastUS-only; escalate to broader team.

I'll execute steps 1–3 now. We'll post periodic telemetry updates to the CRT channel (link in related_links).

Runbook note: watch KV cache hit ratio and token latency for streaming endpoints (token-emit latency).

Laura Bennett
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medispan.com
Date: 2027-05-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike - EastUS cluster

Appreciate the quick responses. Medispan — we authorize the gradual traffic shift to WestUS2 per Soojin/Laura's plan. Marissa here — I'll own customer comms and approval for a one-off service credit if the outage meets our SLA criteria.

Two asks for the team:
- Please confirm expected user-visible degradation window (best estimate).
- Save timestamps/metrics for post-mortem and include estimated lost requests so I can coordinate credit calculation.

Also flagging: if this escalates to >2 hours or data-access patterns are affected, we should loop in Emily (VP Customer Success) and request an executive sync.

Thanks — proceeding with the shift.

— Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency & 5xx spike - EastUS cluster

Thank you — confirmed. We consent to gradual 20% -> 50% shift to WestUS2. We'll be on the bridge (joining now). Please keep the communications thread updated with timestamps and any potential user-facing caveats.

If the situation persists beyond 2 hours, escalate to our CTO (cto@medispan.com).

Sarah Kim

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medispan.com
Date: 2027-05-23T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation summary: Medispan EastUS incident (resolved)

Summary: incident resolved and traffic returned to EastUS after controlled remediation and cache tuning. Timeline (high level):
- 2027-05-21 09:12 PDT: customer reported latency and 5xx spike.
- 09:24–09:48 PDT: initiated WestUS2 ramp to 50% and applied KV TTL extension.
- 10:40 PDT: 5xx rate dropped to baseline; latency returned to acceptable window.
- 11:30 PDT: traffic gradually moved back to EastUS after cache stability confirmed.

Follow-ups/actions:
- Post-mortem published: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/medispan-eastus-2027-05-21 (include detailed root cause, timeline, and compensatory credit calc).
- Short-term: add automated KV cache guardrails to avoid prefix-churn amplification.
- Mid-term: modify routing policy to allow faster circuit-breaker activation for similar patterns.

Attachments: medispan-error-sample-0521.log, traffic-heatmap-eastus-0521.png, runbook-eastus-evacuation-v2.md

Closing notes: Marissa — please proceed with customer compensation per SLA guidelines if the post-mortem shows sustained user impact beyond SLA thresholds. Laura — please schedule a follow-up to review automated guardrail work.

Thanks all for the fast coordination.

— Soojin Lee
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
